_meta.indication: OMNARIS Nasal Spray is indicated for the treatment of nasal symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 401 (4-week seasonal allergic rhinitis pivotal trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled, 4-week single dose-level trial in seasonal allergic rhinitis
pivotal_trials.population: Adolescents and adults 12 years and older with seasonal allergic rhinitis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference from placebo in change from baseline of average AM and PM reflective total nasal symptom score (r-TNSS) averaged over the first 2 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Reflective TNSS difference from placebo -0.90 (95% CI -1.36, -0.45); p<0.001

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 402 (6-week perennial allergic rhinitis pivotal trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter (41 centers, US and Canada), 6-week trial in perennial allergic rhinitis
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 12 years and older with a history of perennial allergic rhinitis and positive allergen skin test
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference from placebo in change from baseline of average AM and PM reflective total nasal symptom score (r-TNSS) over 6 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Reflective TNSS difference from placebo -0.62 (95% CI -0.97, -0.28); p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse events in 2-6 week trials in patients 12 and older (200 mcg vs placebo): headache 6.0% vs 4.6%, epistaxis 4.9% vs 2.9%, nasopharyngitis 3.7% vs 3.3%, ear pain 2.2% vs 0.6%.
target_moa: Ciclesonide is a non-halogenated glucocorticoid pro-drug hydrolyzed in the nasal mucosa to the active metabolite des-ciclesonide (RM1), which has anti-inflammatory activity with glucocorticoid receptor affinity 120 times higher than the parent compound; corticosteroids affect multiple cell types and mediators involved in allergic inflammation.

summary.text: Ciclesonide nasal spray (OMNARIS) is a new molecular entity of the corticosteroid class, reviewed under a standard priority classification and approved first cycle on October 20, 2006 for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in patients 12 and older; no advisory committee was convened, and a deferred PREA pediatric growth study and an HPA-axis safety study were required/committed post-approval.
